vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: icp-filing
Version: 2.3.4

The skill bundle is a legitimate informational tool for ICP filing in China. The scripts (scripts/icp.sh and scripts/script.sh) provide checklists, workflow guides, and basic local data logging without any network access, sensitive data exfiltration, or malicious execution patterns. While there is a minor logic bug in scripts/icp.sh where arguments are not correctly passed to the embedded Python script, there is no evidence of harmful intent or security risk.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with an ICP-filing CLI assistant: it contains local helper scripts, requires no credentials, and only writes user-scoped data files; nothing indicates hidden network exfiltration or unrelated privileges.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (ICP filing guide) align with the included scripts and SKILL.md. The code implements CLI commands for checklists, process flow, footer generation and a small local data utility — all coherent with a filing helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct/perform only local actions (print guidance, generate HTML footer, query instructions). They do reference and print external URLs for official sites, but they do not perform network requests. Note: the scripts read HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME and will create files under the user data dir.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only skill with bundled scripts). Nothing is downloaded or executed from external URLs during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No credentials or secret environment variables are requested. The only environment interaction is optional ICP_FILING_DIR and standard XDG_DATA_HOME/HOME to determine a local data directory — appropriate for a CLI utility that stores user data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no elevated/system-wide changes. The skill creates a per-user data directory (~/.local/share/icp-filing by default) and writes logs and a small data.log; this is expected but persistent — users should be aware it stores any entries added via the tool.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: local CLI helpers and guidance for China ICP filing. Before installing, review the two included scripts (they are short and readable). Be aware it will create a per-user data directory (default: ~/.local/share/icp-filing) and write history.log and data.log there; any data you 'add' with the tool will be stored in that file. The skill does not request credentials or perform network calls, but if you want to avoid writing to your home, set ICP_FILING_DIR to a temporary directory or run it in an isolated environment. If you need higher assurance, verify the author/site links (bytesagain.com) independently before trusting any support endpoints referenced in the documentation.
